extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy of science and physics (educated general readers, philosophers, and physicists)
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length philosophical and scientific analysis arguing that matter is indestructible, motion is continuous, and force persists; examines the conceptual and empirical grounds for these postulates and their consequences (e.g., uniformity of law, transformation of forces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indestructibility of Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter is indestructible; its indestructibility can be inductively inferred and is a necessity of thought — the idea of matter being created or annihilated is a pseud-idea because it cannot be realized in consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument draws on experimental practice (e.g., chemical analysis using scales) and astronomical inference: quantitative science depends on stable units (weights, measures) and the constancy of gravitative force; the chemist's repeated verdict from scales (units of weight/gravitative force) is cited as the empirical basis. Caveat: such inferences presuppose the persistence/constancy of the units of force themselves; circularity must be avoided (cannot assume persistence of force to prove persistence of matter). Examples: conservation inferred from scales in chemistry and from astronomical predictions that assume action/reaction and unchanged forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of Motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion is continuous and never truly begins or ceases; thinking of motion as commencing or stopping is impossible because it would establish a relation between something and nothing in consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support given by both a priori reasoning and empirical inference from forces: examples include sound propagation (vibrations transmitted through air imply force antecedents and consequents), sailors hearing distant bells (inference from impressions to underlying force/motion), and celestial mechanics where motion is inferred from relative positions and laws of force. The principle of equal and opposite reaction is foundational to concluding motion is only transferred, not lost. Mental anti-pattern: imagining stoppage of motion without accounting for correlated force (i.e., neglecting reaction/force transfer) is incoherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence of Force
rubrics_metrics.description: Force persists (the quantity of Force remains always the same); this is an ultimate postulate necessary for science and cannot be established by inductive proof alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter argues this is a fundamental cognition/postulate underlying all quantitative science: without a persistent force, phenomena would be arbitrary and science impossible. It discusses the impossibility of circular proofs (you cannot prove persistence of motion by assuming persistent force and vice versa). Measurement practices (units derived from linear extension, scales) rely on the constancy of force-units; thus many empirical inferences implicitly assume force persistence. The author notes linguistic/terminological issues (preference for 'persistence' over 'conservation') and treats this claim as transcending demonstration while being required by the structure of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Force as an Absolute / Unknowable Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'force' whose persistence is asserted is not the immediate muscular sensation we know, but an Absolute Force — an Unknown Cause transcending our conception; persistence therefore predicates continued existence of an Unknowable power that underlies manifestations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between force as experienced (transient muscular tension) and the metaphysical postulate of a persistent Unknown Cause that grounds observable manifestations. This identification links the scientific postulate with religious/philosophical ultimate reality: both deny knowability of the Absolute but insist on its existence. Use this idea to interpret physical conservation as persistence of an underlying, unobservable power rather than persistence of familiar, cognizable sensations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence of Relations Among Forces (Uniformity of Law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only does force persist, but the relations among forces persist: identical antecedents and conditions yield identical consequents; the uniformity of law follows as an immediate corollary from persistence of force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete illustrations: two equal bullets projected with equal forces will travel equal distances in equal times; explosions with identical charges and conditions produce identical proportions among products (momentum, heat, sound, recoil). Any imagined difference in effects without difference in antecedents implies creation/annihilation of force and is therefore inconceivable. This principle grounds the expectation of reproducibility and constant connexions among phenomena and justifies treating uniformity of law as more than an inductive generalization — as deducible from the datum of persistent force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation and Equivalence of Forces (Energy Transformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manifestations of force that appear to 'end' reappear in new shapes; forces transform into equivalent amounts of other forces (motion ↔ heat ↔ electricity ↔ magnetism ↔ light), providing experimental support for an equivalence doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and experimental support cited (Mayer, Joule, Grove, Helmholtz). Examples include: motion arrested producing heat (rubbing hands, friction igniting brakes), motion producing electricity (frictional experiments, electrical machines, steam-escape devices), magnetism induced by motion or electric currents, light from collisions or electric sparks, and steam engines converting molecular motion (heat) into visible motion. The text treats heat as molecular motion and notes the steam-engine as evidence of molecular motion producing macroscopic motion. Empirical pattern: where forces seemed lost, instrumentation has revealed reappearance in other forms; this supports the doctrine that expenditure undergoes metamorphosis into equivalent other forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and Limitation of Measurement Units in Quantitative Inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative science depends on units (linear measures, balances) and the assumption that these units (and their associated forces, e.g., gravitation of standard weights) are constant; without constancy of units of force, many inferences about matter and motion would be invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chemist's proof of matter's indestructibility relies on scales (units of weight/gravitative force); astronomers' predictions rely on assuming a unit of force for mutual attraction at a distance. The chapter warns that these measurement-based inferences implicitly assume persistence of force-units, and that if such units varied, inferences (equal masses, undiminished motion) could be false. This section functions as a methodological caution about hidden assumptions in empirical measurement and the potential circularity if persistence of force is presupposed.
